vision_report.narrative_description: As the Garden Botanical Observer, my meticulous audit of the chronological image sequence reveals a generally stable and healthy indoor botanical biome, despite significant challenges posed by inconsistent lighting. The Mexican Mint (P2) in its black pot consistently displays two turgid, light green leaves, rooted in what appears to be adequately moist soil. The Money Plant cutting, unmonitored in its white cup, maintains a single, vibrant dark green leaf, propagating successfully in clear water. Over the initial days (EARLIEST to T-3), both specimens showed minor postural adjustments but no signs of distress or decline. A critical interruption occurred at T-2 and CURRENT, where extreme underexposure rendered the entire scene almost completely dark, making any detailed assessment impossible. However, upon the return of visibility in T-1, both plants were observed to have maintained their healthy state, suggesting resilience through the obscured periods. A new white cylindrical object was noted in the background at T-1, representing a 'New Introduction' to the biome. No 'Systemic Losses' or 'Incidental Growth' (weeds, moss) were detected. The visual evidence, though intermittent, points to thriving plant health under the given indoor conditions.
